description:
FILED s543o (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-27) while rebuilding the Rosetta corpus (tools/rosetta-corpus build; docs/rosetta-plan.md section 2).  TOOLING, not a PCL bug: the ADMISSION of tools/everyday-smoke.pl --bless-expect has two holes, both met by the Rosetta corpus of 2026-11-24.

(1) THE CLOCK AT SECOND RESOLUTION.  The three perl runs (twice in place, once a copy at another path) run back to back; a program that prints the time to the second agrees with itself when the three runs fall inside one second.  1442-Text-to-HTML (a Pod::Simple HTML header: generated under perl at <date> GMT) was admitted that way on 2026-11-24 and sat in the corpus as a SILENT differing program that no PCL fix could clear (its .expect holds 'Tue Nov 24 21:25:16 2026').  A COIN FLIP likewise: 0359-Distinct-palindromes-within-decimal-numb prints one of two outputs, half and half (8 runs: 4 and 4; hash order), and its 2 (s493) + 3 (the bless) runs agreed by chance.

(2) THE TIMEOUT IS WHOLE SECONDS.  admit() and run_corpus() test `time() - $start > $timeout` with integer time(), so --timeout 8 kills a run somewhere between 8 and 9+ s: 1107-Pythagorean-triples (8.03 s here) passes --bless-expect --timeout 8, where s493's `timeout 8` refused it.

WHAT s543o DID (Rosetta only): `tools/rosetta-corpus build` re-runs every admitted program once more, minutes later, through the runner's own --verify-with-perl (a DRIFT pass): the clock (anything finer than the build's length) and most coin flips are refused; both programs left the corpus (650; baselines/rosetta-corpus.tsv's header).  And a rebuild no longer re-decides the clock at all (the manifest's programs get 60 s).

OPEN, for the battery's own admission (everyday/): either a drift re-run inside --bless-expect (cost: one more perl run per program, and the gap between runs must exceed a second -- e.g. run 3 only after time() has moved), or document the hole in docs/everyday-battery.md "How a program is admitted".  The battery's 122 programs were written by hand and none prints the clock (its `--verify-with-perl` would show a drift), so this is low priority.  Hole (2) matters only where a timeout is a selection rule (it is not for the battery: 60 s is a safety net); a Time::HiRes-free fix is `select`-polling against a deadline taken from `time` plus one second of slack, or reading /proc/self/stat -- or simply documenting "--timeout S means S to S+1 seconds".
subject: TOOLING: tools/everyday-smoke.pl --bless-expect admits a program whose STDOUT holds the clock (its three runs in one second: 1442-Text-to-HTML) or a coin flip that agreed three times (0359), and its --timeout is whole seconds (--timeout 8 lets 1107 run 8.03 s); tools/rosetta-corpus build closes both for the Rosetta corpus with a drift pass, the battery keeps them
triage_reason: a hole in the measurement tool's admission (no PCL behaviour); the Rosetta half is closed by s543o
